y1: Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain. At that moment, Jesus' face shone like the sun, and His clothes became as white as light. He was transformed.
y2: Moses and Elijah appeared and were talking with Jesus. Then God's voice came from a bright cloud: 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!'
y4: The disciples were very afraid and fell to the ground. Jesus came to them, touched them, and said, 'Get up, and don't be afraid.'
y5: When the disciples looked up, they saw only Jesus. God is not scary; He comes close to us through Jesus.
y7: At the bottom of the mountain, a father knelt before Jesus: 'Lord, have mercy on my son. He often falls into the fire and into the water.' The disciples could not heal him.
y8: Jesus healed the boy. Then He said, 'If you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, "Move from here to there," and it will move.'
y9: The Coin in the Fish's Mouth
y10: The people who collected the temple tax asked Peter, 'Doesn't your teacher pay the tax?'
y11: Jesus said, 'Go to the lake and throw in your line. Open the mouth of the first fish you catch, and you will find a coin. Take it and give it to them for Me and you.' Peter really found the coin!
verse: “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!”
prayer: Dear God, thank You for showing that Jesus is Your beloved Son. Help me to be someone who listens well to Jesus' words. When I am afraid, let me remember Jesus saying, 'Get up, don't be afraid,' and let me give even my small faith to Him. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: transform. It means the appearance changes completely. Jesus' divine glory was shown. Jesus' appearance was transformed with light.
d1: Elijah. He is a great prophet of the Old Testament. He went up to heaven in a chariot of fire. Moses and Elijah appeared.
d2: touch. To feel or pat softly with the hand. Jesus touched the disciples.
d3: mustard seed. It is a very small seed. Faith as small as a mustard seed.
d4: tax. Money given to the government or the temple. They paid the temple tax.
